cards.explanation: The answer is that they welcome them joyfully. The text says, “When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us joyfully.” That's the kind of welcome where somebody grabs your bag before you can ask. Joyfully is the word the text uses, friends.

The answer is what God had done among the Gentiles through him. Gentiles are people who aren't Jews, and Paul recounted what God had done among them through his ministry. Notice whose work he's reporting on, friends. He talks about what God had done. I'd have been so busy bragging about my cookies that I'd have burnt the batch.

The answer is True. The text says that when James and the elders heard Paul's report, they glorified God. They heard what God had done and gave Him the glory. That's a good habit to bake into your own day, friends.

The answer is Moses, Israel's leader. The elders say the believers are under the impression that Paul teaches the Jews among the Gentiles to forsake Moses. Notice they say “under the impression,” friends. That's what they've heard, and it isn't the same as what Paul actually teaches.

The answer is False. The rumor says Paul is telling them not to circumcise their children or observe their customs. Nobody is saying he tells them to keep circumcising, friends. It's a rumor, and the elders say in verse 24 that there's no truth to it.

The answer is to purify himself with them and pay their expenses. The elders tell Paul to take the four men, purify himself along with them and pay their expenses. Pay their expenses, friends! That's like hearing, "You're coming with us, and you're picking up the check." The text says it's so the four can have their heads shaved.

The answer is that the rumors about him are not true. The elders say, “Then everyone will know that there is no truth to these rumors about you…” The plan is to show everyone that the rumors are false, friends. They add that Paul also lives in obedience to the law.

The answer is food sacrificed to idols. The elders' list says the Gentile believers must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals and from sexual immorality. That's four things, friends. They tell Paul they have already written this decision to them.

The answer is to announce the date the offering would be made for each man. Paul enters the temple to give notice of the date when their purification would be complete. That is also when the offering would be made for each of them. It's a notice, friends, like putting a pickup time on a cookie order.

The answer is that they stir up the whole crowd and seize him. The Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul at the temple, stirred up the whole crowd and seized him. That's the turn in this story, friends. From here on, things get hard for Paul.

The answer is bringing Greeks into the temple. The Jews from Asia cry out, “Furthermore, he has brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.” It's a serious thing to say about someone, friends, and the next verse tells us where they got it.

The answer is False. They had seen Trophimus the Ephesian with Paul in the city, and the text says they assumed Paul had brought him into the temple. An assumption is only a guess that got loud, friends. Nobody in the text says they saw Trophimus inside.

The answer is temple. The people seize Paul and drag him out of the temple. After that, the text says the gates were shut at once. That's a hard scene, friends, and I think this part of the story hurts.

The answer is that he runs down with soldiers and centurions. The text says that immediately he took some soldiers and centurions and ran down to the crowd. Centurions are Roman officers, friends. Immediately, and running, is how the text puts it.

The answer is True. The text says that when the people saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul. This is a heavy part of the story, friends. The crowd had been beating him, and now they stop.

The answer is who he is and what he has done. After arresting Paul, the commander asks who he was and what he had done. Those are two fair questions, friends. But the text says the commander could not get at the truth because of the uproar.

The answer is barracks. The commander can't get at the truth because of the uproar, so he orders Paul brought into the barracks. Barracks are where the soldiers stay, friends. I know a little about being carried somewhere you didn't pick.

The answer is because of the violence of the mob. The text says Paul had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob. The soldiers had to lift him, friends. I think this is the hardest picture in the whole passage, so I'm saying it plainly.
